newsitem.title: GERMANY: INSTANT VIEW - German April M3 Money supply.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - German April M3 Money supply.

text.p: The Bundesbank announced that M3 money supply grew an annualised 6.7 percent in April versus the average for the fourth quarter of 1996, down from 8.3 percent growth in March. Following are analysts comments:
PETRA KOEHLER, ECONOMIST, DRESDNER BANK, FRANKFURT:

"We expected 6.8 percent, so that is pretty close to the actual number. We had expected an increase in monetary capital formation after the temporary increase in interest rates in March burdened the bond market."

"We are quite optimistic for economic growth in Germany, 2.8 percent this year and three percent next. We have very low inflation rates which should stay low which is a relief for the bond markets, so monetary capital formation should stay low.

"This is a pretty good number of course and the next M3 figure should now be within the target corridor. The question is what these money supply figures actually mean for monetary policy. The data we are receiving at the moment is good, we could see a figure as low as 6 or even 5.5 percent in the next quarter."
